items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: add live progress (X of X) to the Extract action
items.why: Extracting a batch of missing files gives no feedback until the whole thing finishes -- director's own words: clicking a button with nothing happening always reads as 'is this broken?' The scan step already has this exact streaming-progress pattern; bring it to Extract too.
items.prompt:
Real live feedback: extracting a batch of missing files (Rebuild Missing Files, Step 2 report, 'Extract selected from archive') gives zero indication anything is happening until the whole batch finishes -- director's own words: 'when I click a button and nothing is happening I always wonder if an issue.' This can genuinely take a while for a big batch (just confirmed live extracting all of 'My GTS Audio Overhaul', dozens of mods/hundreds of files).

GROUNDING: this exact tool already has a working streaming-progress pattern one screen over -- the scan itself (`scanSession` in `web/rebuild-missing-routes.js`, `createSseSession` from `./sse-session`, `GET /api/rebuild-missing/scan/events`) streams `mod-scanned` events with `{index, total, collectionName, modName}`, and the client (`rmfHandleScanEvent` in `web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`) renders them as `"{collectionName}: {index} / {total} — {modName}"` in `rmfScanLoadingText`. Mirror this SAME pattern for Extract -- don't invent a new progress mechanism.

SCOPE:
1. `POST /api/rebuild-missing/extract` (`web/rebuild-missing-routes.js` ~line 381): wrap the existing per-item `for (const item of items)` loop with the same SSE session pattern `scanSession` already uses -- a new `extractSession`, emitting a `mod-extracted` (or similar) event per item as it completes: `{index, total, name, ok}`. Same `GET /api/rebuild-missing/extract/events` shape as `/scan/events`.
2. Client (`web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`, the `rmfExtractConfirmOkBtn` click handler ~line 461): instead of a bare `await rmfApi('POST', ...)` with nothing shown until it resolves, show a progress line the same way `rmfScanLoadingText` does -- something like a small inline status area near the Extract button, updating live as each `mod-extracted` event arrives: "{index} / {total} mods restored — {name}". Disable the Extract button and the confirm modal's own OK button while a batch is running, same as the scan already disables its own controls mid-run.
3. Keep the existing final summary callout (`rmfApplyExtractResults`'s success/warning text) as the completion state once the SSE stream reports done -- this is additive progress feedback during the run, not a replacement for the existing result summary.
4. Apply the SAME treatment to Download Archive if it's a multi-item batch action anywhere in this tool (check whether Download Archive is ever called for more than one row at a time) -- if it's always single-row, a plain busy-button state ("Downloading…", already present per the code read for this task) is enough there and doesn't need full SSE progress.

VERIFY live against a real, largish batch (e.g. 'My GTS Audio Overhaul', the same collection just used to confirm the underlying extraction now works after the 413 fix) -- confirm the progress line updates per mod in real time, confirm the final summary still shows correctly once done, and confirm a small/fast batch (1-2 files) doesn't feel janky with the added progress UI (a near-instant complete should still render cleanly, not flash unreadably). Handoff with what you tested.
